title: Separate dynamic DAG qualification from canonical replay fixtures
objective: Prevent a fast static replay graph from being promoted as a deployable DAG, while preserving exact canonical validation and hardware-legal stage boundaries.

rules.statement: A case-dependent upstream boundary must be declared as dag_input before Scheduler or deployment qualification. Embedding canonical values as BAS parameters proves only a replay recipe.
rules.falsification: Reject the rule only for a boundary proven immutable across every supported runtime configuration and explicitly owned as a static parameter.

rules.statement: Keep canonical runtime payloads in case artifacts and materialize a separate validation image at compiler-declared dynamic-input offsets. Do not modify the immutable compiler image or reclassify the values as static parameters.
rules.falsification: Reject any overlay whose name, length, digest or compiler-declared logical type differs from the frozen case manifest.

rules.statement: When a backend field cannot encode a whole graph, split at exact value boundaries so every stage is independently legal; preserve the full ordered payload and include inter-stage transfer cost in integrated qualification.
rules.falsification: Reject if any stage exceeds the field capacity, changes fixed-point data, omits visible bytes, or reports only isolated-task cycles.

rules.statement: Compare all visible outputs in Gem5 fast and verification for both the compiled DAG recipe and the decoded Scheduler L1 recipe. Treat the L1 contract model as descriptor/packaging evidence, not Scheduler firmware execution or RTL evidence.
rules.falsification: Any fast/verification, compiled/L1, intermediate/final or return-port mismatch rejects the candidate.

rules.statement: Use compiler/backend address contracts exactly as declared. A canonical fixture overlay does not establish a universal +0x4000 or -0x4000 pointer translation.
rules.falsification: A translation may be introduced only as a backend-scoped manifest rule backed by dedicated Gem5 and RTL address-conformance evidence.

non_transferable_items: the five selected stage task counts
promotion_conditions: Human review of the distinction between replay and runtime DAG qualification
A second workload family demonstrating the same fixture/runtime separation
An exact shadow patch against current live-registry and skill base digests
Fresh RTL for backend-scoped hardware claims after license restoration

shadow_patch.reason: This turn records workload evidence; live portable promotion requires a second workload and explicit human review.

rollback: Remove this proposal and its index entry; workload validation artifacts remain immutable evidence.
